title: Forcible Removal — Arbitrary Detention, Collusion, and Cover‑Up by PDI and LATAM
category: Arbitrary Detention / Abuse of Authority / Obstruction of Justice
allegation_summary: On 5 July 2024, PDI officers forcibly removed passenger [[SPK-passenger-leandro]] from LATAM flight LA8159 at Santiago Airport solely on the basis of an unverified accusation of aggression by a LATAM [[SPK-stewardess-accuser]]. After the removal, PDI/DGAC officials reviewed CCTV, confirmed no aggression had occurred, and then colluded with LATAM staff to fabricate a post‑hoc justification and conceal the exculpatory evidence. Throughout the following hours, LATAM's security chief and ground staff systematically denied the passenger information, provided a falsified generic report, and applied a false 'disruptive passenger' label that led to a boarding denial the next day. This constitutes arbitrary detention, abuse of public office, obstruction of justice, and a continuing violation of constitutional rights.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Artículo 19 N° 7 — Libertad personal y seguridad individual
verification_required: Confirm this article exists and applies.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Artículo 19 N° 3 — Igual protección de la ley / debido proceso
verification_required: Confirm this article exists and applies.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Artículo 19 N° 1 — Derecho a la vida y a la integridad física y psíquica
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 19 N° 1 CPR from bcn.cl/leychile and confirm applicability to excessive physical force during removal
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If PDI officers used excessive physical force during the forcible removal, the passenger's right to physical and psychological integrity under Art. 19 N° 1 CPR is engaged. The facts suggest physical coercion without proportionate justification.
candidate_articles.history_note: Complementary constitutional provision to Art. 19 N° 7; addresses bodily integrity rather than liberty per se.

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 20 CPR from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that Art. 19 N° 7 is covered by the recurso de protección (note: traditionally Art. 21 habeas corpus covers liberty; verify overlap)
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 20 provides the constitutional action (recurso de protección) for violations of several Art. 19 guarantees. Relevant as a remedial vehicle for the arbitrary act, though liberty deprivation is more typically addressed via Art. 21 (amparo/habeas corpus).

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 21 CPR from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm applicability to short-duration detentions by police at airports
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The specific constitutional remedy for arbitrary arrest or detention. Even though the detention may have been brief, Chilean jurisprudence recognizes amparo for short deprivations of liberty when lacking legal basis.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Artículo 148 Código Penal — Detención ilegal por funcionario público
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 148 CP from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm that PDI officers qualify as 'empleado público' under this provision
Verify whether the article requires a formal detention order or covers de facto deprivation
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Art. 148 CP penalizes the public official who illegally arrests or detains a person. PDI officers are public officials. The CCTV review confirmed no aggression, yet the passenger was forcibly removed and detained. Agent-fit: PDI officers are public employees — this article targets them directly.
candidate_articles.history_note: This article targets the PDI officers (public agents), not the airline. Included because the violation title names PDI as actors.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Artículo 255 Código Penal — Abusos contra particulares por funcionarios públicos
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 255 CP from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm scope covers arbitrary acts by police beyond their authority
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Covers public officials who, abusing their office, commit any arbitrary act or vexation against persons. The PDI officers acted on an airline request without independent verification (later confirmed no aggression on CCTV), potentially constituting an arbitrary act.
candidate_articles.history_note: Targets PDI officers as public agents.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Artículo 330 Código Penal — Violencias innecesarias (fuerza pública)
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 330 CP from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether PDI (civilian police) falls within scope or if limited to Carabineros/military
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Penalizes members of the public force who use unnecessary violence in the performance of their duties. Applicability to PDI (as opposed to Carabineros) must be verified; if PDI qualifies, the forcible removal without proportionate cause is covered.
candidate_articles.history_note: Scope to PDI uncertain — verification critical.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Aeronáutico Art. 100 — Atribuciones del comandante de aeronave
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 100 DFL 221 (Código Aeronáutico) from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether commander's authority to disembark passengers requires objective grounds or mere subjective belief
Verify if Art. 100 or nearby articles impose proportionality requirements
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The Código Aeronáutico grants the aircraft commander authority over passengers, but this authority is not unlimited. If the disembarkation order lacked objective grounds (CCTV later confirmed no aggression), the exercise of this power may have been abusive and ultra vires.
candidate_articles.history_note: Exact article number for commander's disembarkation power needs verification; may be Art. 64, 65, or 100 depending on edition.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Aeronáutico Art. 145 — Responsabilidad del transportador aéreo
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 145 and surrounding articles (Title IX) of DFL 221 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm scope of carrier liability for wrongful denial of boarding or removal
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Establishes the air carrier's liability regime. If the removal was wrongful (no aggression confirmed), LATAM may bear civil liability under the aeronautical liability framework in addition to general tort law.
candidate_articles.history_note: Exact article number for carrier liability for wrongful removal needs verification within Title IX of the Código Aeronáutico.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Artículo 2314 Código Civil — Responsabilidad extracontractual (delito/cuasidelito civil)
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 2314 CC from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm applicability to both LATAM (as instigator of removal) and PDI (as executor)
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: General tort liability: whoever commits a delict or quasi-delict causing damage to another is obliged to indemnify. Applicable to both the airline (for requesting removal without basis) and potentially the State (for PDI's execution of the removal with excessive force).

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Artículo 2320 Código Civil — Responsabilidad por el hecho ajeno
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 2320 CC from bcn.cl/leychile
Assess whether LATAM bears vicarious liability for crew's false accusation that triggered PDI intervention
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Vicarious liability of LATAM for the acts of its crew members (stewardess who made the accusation triggering the removal). The airline is responsible for damage caused by persons under its care or direction.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley 19.496 Art. 3 — Derechos básicos del consumidor
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 3 Ley 19.496 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm applicability of consumer protection framework to air transport contracts
Identify specific letters (a, b, c, d, e) most relevant to dignitary and safety rights
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Establishes basic consumer rights including the right to safety, right to non-discrimination, and right to dignified treatment. The forcible removal based on a false accusation may violate the passenger's consumer rights under this provision.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley 19.496 Art. 23 — Infracción por negativa injustificada de venta o prestación de servicio
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for Art. 23 Ley 19.496 from bcn.cl/leychile
Confirm whether wrongful removal from a flight constitutes 'negativa injustificada de prestación de servicio'
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: Removing a passenger from a flight without justified cause may constitute an unjustified refusal to provide the contracted service (air transport), triggering consumer-law sanctions.
